hazard: Absence of documented fitness-to-transfer process and medication arrangements
theme: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

reports.title: Redmond Johnson
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: If a detainee has a history of significant medical problems, healthcare professionals undertaking the initial reception assessment should request further information from the General Practitioner and, where necessary, hospital doctors normally involved in the detainee's care to enable appropriate care planning while that detainee is in the custody of the prison service.
concerns.hazard: failure to obtain medical history from GP and hospital doctors

concerns.quote: Information about which detainees are going to be transferred to court or other locations needs to be delivered to the individual prisons in enough time for a thorough assessment of the detainee's fitness to be transferred (including a face to face assessment if required) to be conducted.

There must be a robust and clearly documented process in place when assessing a detainee's fitness to transfer, together with clear arrangements made in respect of any medication that the detainee needs to take while out of the prison's care.
concerns.hazard: absence of documented fitness-to-transfer process and medication arrangements

concerns.quote: Medication reviews should be conducted, with appropriate pharmacy input if required, if there are complex medication issues that need resolving or clarifying.
concerns.hazard: inadequate medication review for complex regimens

concerns.quote: Reception healthcare should ask about any outstanding hospital or other healthcare appointments and rebook these if necessary.
concerns.hazard: failure to coordinate ongoing healthcare appointments

concerns.quote: If medical tests or investigations are requested, there must be clear and adequate documentation to confirm that those investigations have actually been conducted and the results seen by a healthcare professional.

reports.title: Jonathan McCarthy: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: There was no evidence that HMP Altcourse took any steps to verify this appointment
There was no evidence that HMP Thameside took any steps to verify this appointment

It was suggested in evidence that HMP Thameside automatically re-arrange all community medical appointments for security reasons. It was clarified that the prison would only try to get a new appointment if there was a specific security concern
concerns.hazard: automatic rescheduling of medical appointments without clinical assessment

concerns.quote: There was also no evidence that Mr McCarthy had a fitness to transfer assessment at either HMP Altcourse or HMP Thameside
concerns.hazard: absence of fitness to transfer assessment

concerns.quote: assessing fitness to transfer and determining medical hold

links.explanation: Both reports highlight the absence of a proper fitness-to-transfer assessment for detainees before movement. They share the concern that without such assessment, risks to health are not managed.
